summary: In major commercial launch news, Chinese firm LandSpace successfully recovered a Zhuque-3 rocket booster following its second orbital flight, marking the private vehicle's second touchdown. In military space developments, the U.S. Space Force and Japan launched a second U.S. military sensor payload aboard a Japanese satellite to enhance space domain awareness over the Indo-Pacific. Aboard the International Space Station, a NASA astronaut and the first French female spacewalker successfully removed a failed antenna, though time ran out before they could install its replacement. Nearby, NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter captured new images of a Falcon 9 impact crater on the moon, offering fresh insights into lunar surface collisions. Defense and policy updates saw the Department of Defense expand research and development on clearing defunct satellites from orbit, while the European Union levied new sanctions targeting leaders of Russia’s space industry. In commercial leadership, United Launch Alliance appointed a new chief executive officer, and the National Reconnaissance Office announced plans to expand its use of HawkEye 360’s commercial satellite intelligence. Readers should watch tonight for SpaceX’s scheduled attempt to conduct its 100th launch of the year.
